title: Number of Ways to Reach a Position After Exactly k Steps
summary: Given positive integers startPos and endPos, calculate the number of distinct ways to reach endPos from startPos in exactly k steps on an infinite number line.
statement: Given positive integers startPos and endPos, calculate the number of distinct ways to reach endPos from startPos in exactly k steps on an infinite number line. Each step can be either left or right. The result is modulo 10^9 + 7. Different ways are distinct if the sequence of steps differs.
constraints: Each of exactly k steps moves one position left or right on an infinite number line.
Two ways differ when their left/right step sequences differ.
Return the number ending at end_pos modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Let r be the number of right steps and l the number of left steps.
If the distance is too large or parity is wrong, return zero; otherwise choose which r of the k steps go right.
Every valid sequence corresponds uniquely to a choice of right-step positions, so the binomial coefficient counts exactly all ways.
editorial: Every valid sequence corresponds uniquely to a choice of right-step positions, so the binomial coefficient counts exactly all ways.

tests.explanation: Two right steps and one left step can be ordered in three distinct ways, so the answer is three.
The distance and step-count parity differ, making the destination unreachable in exactly ten steps.
